problems_active.text: Invasive breast cancer, right, NST type G2, HER2 3+/HR+, cT2N1M0 (stage IIB), neoadjuvant chemotherapy ongoing
Status after thyroidectomy (benign goitre), permanent levothyroxine replacement

past_history.text: Benign multinodular goitre, total thyroidectomy 06/2015 (histology: no malignancy)
Neutropenic fever after EC cycle 3 (April 2024), treated in hospital with piperacillin/tazobactam and G-CSF

medication_at_discharge.dose: 125 mg day 1, 80 mg days 2+3 (with each cycle)
300 µg subcutaneously daily from cycle day 2 (primary prophylaxis, 7 days)

medication_stopped_during_stay.reason: Not effective enough after cycle 1; replaced by triple antiemetic therapy (aprepitant + ondansetron + dexamethasone)
Treatment of neutropenic fever, stopped after 48 h without fever
Therapeutic for the neutropenia episode, stopped after recovery; then newly ordered as primary prophylaxis from cycle 4

procedures.text: Port catheter implanted, right (Bard PowerPort, 8F, titanium), right subclavian vein
EC chemotherapy cycles 1–4 (epirubicin 90 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m²)
MRI liver with contrast: liver lesion in segment VII classified as cavernous haemangioma

medical_devices_implants.text: Fully implantable central venous catheter (Port-a-Cath®, Bard PowerPort, 8F, titanium reservoir), right subclavian vein, tip in the superior vena cava

P005-D001.title: Discharge letter after thyroidectomy
P005-D001.text:
Dear colleagues,
We report on the stay of Mrs Monika Steinbauer, born 11.09.1966, from 19.06.2015 to 22.06.2015.

Diagnosis: benign multinodular goitre (E04.2), total thyroidectomy indicated because of progression and local compression symptoms.

Operation (19.06.2015): total thyroidectomy. Histology: benign multinodular hyperplasia, no malignancy.

Course: no complications. Calcium borderline after surgery (2.02 mmol/l), temporary calcium replacement. Vocal cord check: ENT normal.

Medication at discharge:
- Levothyroxine 100 µg (Euthyrox) 1-0-0 (hormone replacement, permanent)
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg + vitamin D3 200 IU, 1-0-1 (for 4 weeks, until TSH and calcium are normal)

Allergies: none known.
Family history: mother died of breast cancer at 64.
Recommendation: endocrinology check in 6 weeks (TSH, fT4).
Kind regards, Senior Dr Werner Pirker, surgery

P005-D002.title: First oncology visit – breast cancer
P005-D002.text:
First oncology visit, 08.02.2024
Patient: Steinbauer Monika, born 11.09.1966, female

Referral: from gynaecology after diagnosis of right breast cancer.

Biopsy (05.02.2024): invasive breast cancer, right, NST type (no special type), G2.
IHC: ER positive (Allred 7/8), PR positive (Allred 6/8), HER2 3+ (FISH confirmed) → luminal B / HER2-positive.
Clinical TNM: cT2 cN1 cM0 (stage IIB).

Previous illnesses:
- Thyroidectomy 06/2015 (benign goitre), levothyroxine 100 µg permanently
- Arterial hypertension (amlodipine 5 mg 1-0-0 since 2020)
Allergies: none known.
Family history: mother with breast cancer (died at 64).

Tumour board (06.02.2024): neoadjuvant chemotherapy + anti-HER2 recommended: EC × 4 (epirubicin 90 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m²) → paclitaxel + trastuzumab × 4, then surgery.

Planned approach:
1. Port catheter before the first cycle
2. EC protocol cycles 1–4
3. Then paclitaxel + trastuzumab × 4
4. Surgery after neoadjuvant therapy

Patient informed, consent obtained.

P005-D003.title: Surgery report: port catheter, right
P005-D003.text:
Surgery report
Date: 19.02.2024
Surgeon: Dr Sandra Hollinger, surgeon
Anaesthesia: local anaesthesia + sedation

Indication: cancer chemotherapy, venous access needed.

Operation: implantation of a fully implantable central venous catheter (Port-a-Cath®, model Bard PowerPort, 8F, titanium reservoir) via the right subclavian vein. Catheter tip in the superior vena cava, correct position.
Fluoroscopy during surgery: correct catheter position, no pneumothorax.

Complications: none.
After surgery: chest X-ray ordered.

Diagnosis: uncomplicated right port catheter placement for cancer therapy.

P005-D004.title: Chest X-ray after port catheter placement
P005-D004.text:
Report: chest X-ray AP, 19.02.2024
Patient: Steinbauer Monika, born 11.09.1966

Clinical question: check port catheter position.

Findings:
Port generator right infraclavicular. Catheter tip in the superior vena cava, correct position. No pneumothorax. No haemothorax.
Heart and lungs: normal. No pleural effusion.
Hila: normal. Mediastinum normal.

Assessment: correct port catheter position. No sign of complications.

P005-D005.title: EC cycle 1 day 1 – start of chemotherapy
P005-D005.text:
26.02.2024, 08:00, Dr Beatrix Langer
EC cycle 1, day 1.

Mrs Steinbauer, 58 years, right breast cancer cT2N1M0, HER2+/HR+.
Good general condition. ECOG 0. Body surface area 1.72 m². Weight 67 kg.
Allergies: none known.

Preparation:
- Antiemetics: ondansetron 8 mg IV 30 min before chemo + dexamethasone 8 mg IV
- Epirubicin 90 mg/m² (= 155 mg) IV via port, 15 min infusion
- Cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² (= 1032 mg) IV via port, 30 min infusion

Tolerance: good. No acute reaction. Mild nausea after the infusion NRS 2.

Continue home medication: levothyroxine 100 µg, amlodipine 5 mg.
Antiemetics at home: ondansetron 8 mg orally 1-1-1 for 3 days.
G-CSF prophylaxis: not ordered (risk <20% with EC, older risk assessment).

Next cycle: 18.03.2024.

P005-D006.title: Nursing report: phone call after cycle 1
P005-D006.text:
28.02.2024, 15:00, registered nurse Karin Moser (phone documentation)

Mrs Steinbauer calls: still nauseous (NRS 3), vomited twice yesterday. Took ondansetron, moderately effective.
She also reports: she does not tolerate ibuprofen – it always gives her stomach problems and once she was "all swollen up". She does not know whether it is a real allergy or an intolerance. She never takes it any more.
Recorded in the patient file and reported to the treating doctor.
No fever. Temperature 36.9°C.
Advice: continue ondansetron; with fever >38°C come to the clinic immediately.

P005-D007.title: Outpatient check after cycle 1 – antiemetic change
P005-D007.text:
04.03.2024, 09:00, Dr Langer
Outpatient check after EC cycle 1.

Patient reports: nausea was marked, vomited twice, ondansetron alone was not enough.
Ibuprofen intolerance reported by the patient (nursing report 28.02.) – recorded as an intolerance (no formal allergy, no systemic reaction confirmed, most likely gastrointestinal intolerance + possibly a pseudo-allergic reaction). Ibuprofen and NSAIDs in general noted in the patient file as a caution.

Antiemetic change for cycle 2:
Ondansetron 8 mg orally alone is not enough → extend to TRIPLE antiemetic therapy:
- Aprepitant 125 mg orally day 1, 80 mg days 2+3
- Ondansetron 8 mg IV (day 1, before chemo) + dexamethasone
- Ondansetron orally as needed at home

Lab (today): leucocytes 3.8 G/l (slightly low, expected after chemotherapy), Hb 11.9 g/dl, platelets 186 G/l. Creatinine 0.74 mg/dl, Na 138, K 3.9. TSH 1.4 mIU/l (levothyroxine replacement adequate).

Next cycle: 18.03.2024 as planned.

P005-D008.title: EC cycle 2 day 1
P005-D008.text:
18.03.2024, 08:00, Dr Langer
EC cycle 2, day 1.

Good general condition. ECOG 0. Hair loss started (expected). The patient is distressed by it; conversation held.
Lab before chemo (18.03.): leucocytes 4.2 G/l, Hb 11.4 g/dl, platelets 198 G/l, creatinine 0.72 mg/dl → cycle possible.

TRIPLE antiemetics (as planned):
- Aprepitant 125 mg orally already taken at home.
- Dexamethasone 8 mg IV + ondansetron 8 mg IV before chemo.
- Epirubicin 90 mg/m² (= 155 mg) IV via port + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² (= 1032 mg) IV.

Tolerance: nausea only NRS 1–2. Much better than cycle 1.
G-CSF: still not ordered.
Next cycle: 08.04.2024.

P005-D009.title: EC cycle 3 day 1 – liver ultrasound abnormal
P005-D009.text:
08.04.2024, 08:00, Dr Langer
EC cycle 3, day 1.

The patient reports occasional tingling in her fingertips for 2–3 weeks and asks whether this could be nerve damage. No in-house neurology examination done. No objective neurological finding. Epirubicin is not a leading neurotoxin (paclitaxel comes later). Entry: patient reports finger tingling, not clinically confirmed, no intervention.

Abdominal ultrasound (staging check, 05.04.):
Finding: round liver lesion (hypoechoic, 1.4 cm, segment VII) → differential metastasis vs. haemangioma. Liver MRI recommended.

Lab before the cycle (08.04.): leucocytes 3.6 G/l (borderline), Hb 10.8 g/dl, platelets 162 G/l, creatinine 0.76 → cycle possible.

Chemo: epirubicin 155 mg + cyclophosphamide 1032 mg IV via port. Triple antiemetics as in cycle 2.
G-CSF: still not ordered (senior doctor decision: leucocytes >3.5 G/l → not needed).

P005-D010.title: Liver MRI – liver lesion work-up
P005-D010.text:
Report: MRI abdomen/liver with contrast (gadolinium), 15.04.2024
Patient: Steinbauer Monika, born 11.09.1966

Clinical question: liver lesion segment VII on ultrasound, metastasis vs. haemangioma with known breast cancer.

Findings:
Liver: round lesion 1.4 cm in segment VII. Signal: T1 hypointense, T2 hyperintense; contrast: early arterial peripheral nodular enhancement, complete fill-in in the delayed phase. Typical haemangioma pattern.
No other focal liver lesions. No lymphadenopathy.
Gallbladder, spleen, pancreas, kidneys: normal.

Assessment:
Liver lesion segment VII: morphology and contrast behaviour clearly consistent with a **cavernous haemangioma**. No sign of a liver metastasis.

Recommendation: no further work-up or biopsy needed. The finding is benign.

P005-D011.title: Progress after cycle 3 – liver lesion benign, G-CSF discussion
P005-D011.text:
19.04.2024, 08:00, Dr Langer

Liver MRI result: haemangioma, no longer suspicious for metastasis → very relieving for the patient. Result communicated.

The patient still reports finger tingling – still not clinically objectifiable.

Lab today (done externally on 17.04.): leucocytes 0.8 G/l ↓↓↓ → severe neutropenia!
Discussed with the senior doctor: the earlier decision "G-CSF not needed" was based on leucocytes >3.5 G/l on the cycle day → now massive neutropenia on day 11 after cycle 3. G-CSF (filgrastim 300 µg subcutaneously daily) started today.

Patient instructed: fever >38°C → go to the emergency department immediately.

P005-D012.title: Emergency admission: neutropenic fever
P005-D012.text:
22.04.2024, 03:30 – emergency admission
Patient: Steinbauer Monika, born 11.09.1966

Presentation: fever 38.9°C, chills, exhaustion. Last chemotherapy (EC cycle 3) on 08.04.2024. Filgrastim subcutaneously since 19.04.

Status:
Temp 38.9°C. BP 108/64 mmHg. Pulse 104/min. SpO2 97%.
General condition reduced, pale, sweating.
Lungs: vesicular both sides, no crackles. Abdomen: soft, not tender.
Port: entry site calm.
No clinical focus found.

Immediate measures:
- Lab STAT
- Blood cultures x2 (peripheral + port)
- Broad-spectrum antibiotic: piperacillin/tazobactam 4.5 g IV every 8 h, start now.
- Continue filgrastim.
- Admit.

Diagnosis: neutropenic fever during chemotherapy (EC cycle 3, day 14) (D70).

P005-D013.title: Emergency laboratory, neutropenic fever
P005-D013.text:
Patient: Steinbauer Monika, born 11.09.1966
Order number: LM-2024-04-22-0014
Sample taken: 22.04.2024, 03:45 (STAT)

Blood count:
  Hb: 9.8 g/dl ↓
  Leucocytes: 0.4 G/l ↓↓↓ [ref: 4.0–10.0]
  Absolute neutrophils: 0.08 G/l ↓↓↓ → severe neutropenia
  Platelets: 88 G/l ↓

Clinical chemistry:
  CRP: 142 mg/l ↑↑
  PCT: 1.8 ng/ml ↑ → bacterial infection likely
  Creatinine: 0.82 mg/dl, Na: 136, K: 3.5

Blood cultures: taken, result pending.

Comment: severe neutropenia with fever – neutropenic sepsis not excluded. STAT result.

P005-D014.title: Progress day 2 – fever falling, blood culture result
P005-D014.text:
24.04.2024, 09:00, Senior Dr Christina Wallner

Patient much better. No fever since yesterday evening 21:00.
BP 118/72, pulse 88/min, temp 37.1°C.

Blood culture result (peripheral + port): both sterile → no bacteraemia found.
Continue piperacillin/tazobactam until 48 h without fever (i.e. until the evening of 25.04.).

Lab (23.04.):
  Leucocytes 1.2 G/l (rising on G-CSF), neutrophils 0.4 G/l
  CRP 88 mg/l (falling), PCT 0.6 ng/ml
  Platelets 102 G/l

Continue filgrastim until neutrophils >1.0 G/l on 2 consecutive days.

Plan: discharge once leucocytes >1.5 G/l and no fever.

P005-D015.title: Progress day 4 – discharge
P005-D015.text:
26.04.2024, 10:00, Dr Langer

Leucocytes 3.1 G/l, neutrophils 2.2 G/l → sufficiently recovered.
No fever for >48 h. Good general condition.
Piperacillin/tazobactam stopped yesterday evening (48 h after the last fever).
Filgrastim: last dose this morning (neutrophils >1.0 G/l on 2 days).

For cycle 4 (planned 29.04.): G-CSF as primary prophylaxis from day 2 (filgrastim 300 µg subcutaneously/day × 7 days) because of this neutropenia episode. Epirubicin dose unchanged (senior doctor decision).

Discharged after 4 days in hospital.

Medication at discharge (after the neutropenia episode):
- Levothyroxine 100 µg 1-0-0 (long-term)
- Amlodipine 5 mg 1-0-0 (long-term)
- Aprepitant 125 mg day 1 / 80 mg days 2+3 (for cycle 4)
- Ondansetron 8 mg as needed (reserve antiemetic)
- Filgrastim 300 µg subcutaneously from cycle 4 day 2 (primary prophylaxis, prescription given)

P005-D016.title: EC cycle 4 day 1 – last EC cycle
P005-D016.text:
29.04.2024, 08:00, Dr Langer
EC cycle 4 (last), day 1.

Recovered from the neutropenia episode. Good general condition. ECOG 1 (slightly reduced by tiredness).
Lab (29.04.): leucocytes 5.2 G/l, Hb 10.2 g/dl, platelets 220 G/l, creatinine 0.78 → cycle possible.

Chemo: epirubicin 155 mg + cyclophosphamide 1032 mg IV via port. Triple antiemetics.
G-CSF: filgrastim 300 µg subcutaneously from tomorrow (day 2), 7 days – primary prophylaxis as planned.

The patient asks again about tingling in her fingers – unchanged, mild. Senior doctor decision: the neuropathy symptom is neither clinically confirmed nor objectifiable (epirubicin is not a typical neurotoxin). No action needed before switching to paclitaxel, where neuropathy can be expected.

Next phase: paclitaxel + trastuzumab × 4 from about June 2024.

P005-D017.title: Nursing report, cycle 4
P005-D017.text:
29.04.2024, 16:00, registered nurse Karin Moser

Mrs Steinbauer, chemotherapy day clinic, cycle 4. Infusion via port without complications.
Tired but cooperative. No nausea with the improved antiemetics.
Port entry site after puncture: dry, calm.
No fever (36.8°C). SpO2 98%.
Wears a wig. Complete hair loss.
No further nursing needs.
